Invited talks, conference presentations, lectures, workshops, panels, and
other public presentations related to my research and professional
activities.

This section is being developed as a chronological and thematic record of
academic and technical presentations given throughout my career.

## Invited Talks & Keynotes

Invited presentations provide an opportunity to discuss research results,
emerging technologies, and broader developments in information security and
digital trust.

Topics have included:

- information security and cryptography;
- digital signatures and public key infrastructure;
- digital identity;
- electronic documents and digital preservation;
- blockchain and cryptocurrencies;
- post-quantum cryptography;
- artificial intelligence and security;
- trustworthy digital infrastructures.

Public slides, videos, proceedings, or event pages will be linked whenever
they are available.

## Conference Presentations

Presentations associated with scientific publications will progressively be
connected to their corresponding bibliographic records.

A presentation record may include:

- event;
- presentation title;
- date and location;
- authors or presenters;
- associated publication;
- slides;
- video;
- event program;
- persistent archival copy.

## Workshops & Tutorials

This section will include longer educational and technical presentations,
such as workshops, tutorials, training activities, and specialized courses.

These materials are particularly useful for preserving the evolution of
technical subjects and the way research results were communicated to
different audiences.

## Panels & Roundtables

Participation in panels and roundtables often documents discussions that do
not appear in conventional academic publications.

Where appropriate, records will include the event, topic, participants,
program, presentation material, and publicly available recordings.

## Institutional & Professional Talks

Some presentations are associated with research projects, public
institutions, professional communities, standards activities, or technology
transfer rather than with a specific scientific publication.

These presentations form part of the broader record of the interaction
between academic research and operational digital infrastructures.

## Teaching & Guest Lectures

Selected guest lectures and presentations given outside regular courses may
also be preserved here when they represent substantial or reusable academic
material.

Regular course material remains organized under [Teaching](teaching.qmd).

## Presentation Archive

Over the years, presentation material has existed in several formats,
including slides, PDFs, event websites, recordings, and institutional
archives.

The long-term objective is to preserve significant presentations together
with enough metadata to establish:

**what was presented → where → when → in which context → related research**

Whenever possible, original presentation files and public PDF versions will
be preserved alongside the descriptive record.
